batch_node.name: gitlab page v0.1.0
batch_node.description: The /gitlab page (req-gitlab-page): the deployment graph (projection, elevation, layout module, scene searches), the posture strip, and the operator tables with their searches. Every search takes ?instance=<name>.

node.name: gitlab deployment layout
node.description: Draws each GitLab instance in the scene as one box: ingress on the left, the processes nested in the compute service each runs on, the runners under them, data stores to the right, sign-in and audit last, and trusted identity providers and event sinks outside the box. Every placement is derived from the vocabulary's edges, never from an entity id, so any page whose scene holds GitLab nodes can use it (req-gitlab-layout).

node.name: gitlab deployment projection

node.name: GitLab deployment
node.description: The instance as deployed: load balancers on the left, each GitLab process inside the compute service it runs on (Gitaly on its own, with its volume), the runner managers and where they launch jobs underneath, the databases, Redis, object stores and secrets it reaches on the right, and the identity provider it trusts and the sinks its audit events land in outside the box. Every box and line is a grid edge; nothing is drawn from a picture.

node.name: GitLab posture
node.description: Which instance the page shows, then one tile per posture question an operator of a FedRAMP 20x environment answers first. A tile reads a count, clear, or not observed (the grid holds none of that type for the instance), never a zero it cannot vouch for.

tiles.label: Components reporting degraded or unhealthy
tiles.help: GitLab components and Gitaly nodes whose last health verdict was degraded or unhealthy. The second number counts those whose health has never been observed — unknown, not healthy.
population: WHERE c.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND c.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance
finding: WHERE c.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND c.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND c.data.health IN ["degraded", "unhealthy"]

secondary.label: health not observed
query: WHERE c.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND c.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND c.data.health = ""

tiles.label: Gitaly on unsupported storage
tiles.help: Gitaly nodes whose repositories sit on NFS or EFS. GitLab supports only local block storage (an attached EBS volume) for Gitaly.
population: WHERE g.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND g.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance
finding: WHERE g.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND g.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND e.data.properties.filesystem IN ["nfs", "efs"]

tiles.label: Instance runners open to any job
tiles.help: Instance-scoped runners that take untagged jobs from unprotected refs: any project's pipeline, including a fork's merge request, can run on them.
population: WHERE r.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND r.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance
finding: WHERE r.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND r.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND r.data.runner_type = "instance_type" AND r.data.run_untagged = true AND r.data.access_level = "not_protected"

tiles.label: Runner managers running jobs privileged
tiles.help: Runner managers configured to run jobs privileged. A privileged job can escape to its host and read other jobs' secrets. Read from config.toml; the GitLab API does not expose it, so the second number is those never observed.
population: WHERE m.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND m.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance
finding: WHERE m.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND m.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND m.data.privileged = true

secondary.label: not observed
query: WHERE m.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND m.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND m.data.privileged IS NULL

tiles.label: CI/CD variables not protected
tiles.help: Variables every pipeline receives, including those on unprotected branches. The second number counts variables GitLab does not mask in job logs.
population: WHERE v.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND v.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance
finding: WHERE v.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND v.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND v.data.protected = false

secondary.label: not masked
query: WHERE v.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND v.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND v.data.masked = false

tiles.label: Access tokens that never expire
tiles.help: Active personal, group, project and impersonation tokens with no expiry date. The second number counts active tokens expiring in the next 30 days.
population: WHERE t.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND t.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance
finding: WHERE t.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND t.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND t.data.expires = false AND (t.data.revoked = false OR t.data.revoked IS NULL)

secondary.label: expire within 30 days
query: WHERE t.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND t.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND t.data.expires_at != "" AND t.data.expires_at < $cutoff AND (t.data.revoked = false OR t.data.revoked IS NULL)

tiles.label: Deploy keys that never expire
tiles.help: Deploy keys with no expiry. The second number counts keys some project lets push.
population: WHERE k.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND k.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance
finding: WHERE k.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND k.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND k.data.expires = false

secondary.label: with write access
query: WHERE k.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND k.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND e.data.properties.can_push = true

tiles.label: Protected branches allowing force-push
tiles.help: Protected-branch rules that still allow force-push, which rewrites history the protection was meant to keep.
population: WHERE b.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND b.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance
finding: WHERE b.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND b.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND b.data.allow_force_push = true

tiles.label: Projects accepting any job token
tiles.help: Projects whose CI_JOB_TOKEN inbound allowlist is off: a job in any project on the instance can use its token against them.
population: WHERE p.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND p.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance
finding: WHERE p.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND p.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND p.data.job_token_inbound_enabled = false

tiles.label: Active people without GitLab 2FA
tiles.help: Active human accounts with no GitLab two-factor authentication. Where sign-in goes only through an SSO provider that enforces MFA, this is expected; the SSO table says whether it does.
population: WHERE u.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND u.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND u.data.user_type = "human"
finding: WHERE u.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND u.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND u.data.user_type = "human" AND u.data.state = "active" AND u.data.two_factor_enabled = false

tiles.label: Administrators
tiles.help: Accounts with instance administrator rights. Not a finding by itself; the number an assessor asks for first.
population: WHERE u.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND u.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance
finding: WHERE u.data.instance_name STARTS_WITH $instance AND u.data.instance_name ENDS_WITH $instance AND u.data.is_admin = true

tiles.label: Password sign-in on the web
tiles.help: Instances that still accept a password on the web sign-in page. With SSO in place, password sign-in is the path around it.
population: WHERE i.data.name STARTS_WITH $instance AND i.data.name ENDS_WITH $instance
finding: WHERE i.data.name STARTS_WITH $instance AND i.data.name ENDS_WITH $instance AND i.data.password_auth_enabled_for_web = true

secondary.label: not observed
query: WHERE i.data.name STARTS_WITH $instance AND i.data.name ENDS_WITH $instance AND i.data.password_auth_enabled_for_web IS NULL

tiles.label: Instances streaming audit events
tiles.help: Instances with at least one destination observed active. Streaming is an Ultimate feature; a Community Edition instance must ship audit_json.log another way, and reads zero here.
population: WHERE i.data.name STARTS_WITH $instance AND i.data.name ENDS_WITH $instance
finding: WHERE i.data.name STARTS_WITH $instance AND i.data.name ENDS_WITH $instance AND d.data.active = true
